chunks: Ibn Nuh said: Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad informed us

He said: Muhammad ibn Nasir al-Namiri was among the companions of Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him). When Abu Muhammad died, Muhammad claimed the position of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman, saying that he was the owner (deputy) of the Imam of the Age, and he claimed for himself the 'Babiyya' (gateway). Allah the Exalted disgraced him through what appeared from him of deviation and ignorance, and Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman cursed him, disowned him, and veiled himself from him, and he claimed that authority after the Shari'i.

key_terms.الإلحاد: Deviation or straying from the truth
key_terms.البابية: The status of being the 'gate' or gateway to the Imam
key_terms.الشريعي: Referring to Muhammad ibn Uthman, known as 'al-Shari'i' (the one who opened the door)
key_terms.صاحب الإمام: The deputy or representative of the Imam

ai.seo_question: Who was Muhammad ibn Nasir al-Namiri and what false claim did he make regarding the Imam's deputyship?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the posthumous claim of Muhammad ibn Nasir al-Namiri to the deputyship of the Imam of the Age, following the death of Muhammad ibn Uman. It highlights the theological significance of the 'Babuniyya' (Gate-ship) doctrine, illustrating how Ibn Nasir’s subsequent exposure of his own ignorance and deviation served as divine validation of the previous deputy’s authority. The text underscores the critical Shia criterion of distinguishing true deputies from false claimants through their adherence to the Imam’s teachings and the Imam’s own disavowal.
